source: USGS 3DEP 1 m (NC QL2 LiDAR) via ImageServer getSamples, 2026-09-07; one section per reach at (or just above) the pour point, perpendicular to the channel heading found on a 4 m thalweg grid; stations 1 m apart; elevations ft NAVD88; LiDAR returns the water surface in the channel

CC-UP-503.name: Mountain (Upper Cullowhee) pour point
CC-UP-503.heading: N
CC-UP-503.slope_note: thalweg water surface 2660.7 -> 2650.2 ft over 60 m of the 4 m grid; steep headwater ravine
CC-UP-503.geom: V-shaped ravine: water ~4 m wide, both sides climbing 10+ ft within 10 m
CC-UP-503.bed_note: unseen bed depth chosen so the flow at the LiDAR survey water surface is ~1-2x the engine baseflow (the survey was flown at ordinary flow); 1 ft on the mainstem, less on the small branches

CC-MS-1100.name: Lower Mountain (mainstem above Speedwell) pour point
CC-MS-1100.heading: N24W
CC-MS-1100.geom: ~6 m channel, banks +2.6 ft, broad valley floor at +1.5-2.7 ft both sides
CC-MS-1100.bed_note: unseen bed depth chosen so the flow at the LiDAR survey water surface is ~1-2x the engine baseflow (the survey was flown at ordinary flow); 1 ft on the mainstem, less on the small branches

CC-TIL-705.name: Tilley Creek, 20 m above its confluence with the mainstem
CC-TIL-705.heading: N56E
CC-TIL-705.slope_note: 2150.0 -> 2148.75 ft over 43 m along Tilley Creek (4 m grid); the pour point itself is at the confluence
CC-TIL-705.geom: ~4 m channel, banks +2.0-2.5 ft, flat floodplain at +2.5 ft
CC-TIL-705.bed_note: unseen bed depth chosen so the flow at the LiDAR survey water surface is ~1-2x the engine baseflow (the survey was flown at ordinary flow); 1 ft on the mainstem, less on the small branches

CC-COX-097.name: Cox Branch, ~55 m above its pour point (the incised reach; at the mouth the branch fans out onto the mainstem floodplain)
CC-COX-097.heading: N38W
CC-COX-097.slope_note: 2097.0 -> 2094.8 ft over 46 m along the branch (4 m grid); noisy
CC-COX-097.geom: ~7 m incised channel at 2095.6, right bank/terrace +3.3 ft (2098.9), left side climbing to a road at +10 ft
CC-COX-097.bed_note: unseen bed depth chosen so the flow at the LiDAR survey water surface is ~1-2x the engine baseflow (the survey was flown at ordinary flow); 1 ft on the mainstem, less on the small branches

CC-LB-171.name: Long Branch pour point
CC-LB-171.heading: N43W
